findings.title: Missing revoke instruction leads to Old delegate accounts have unlimited number of token allowance
findings.description: The Restaking and Vault programs delegate token authority by calling the `approve` instruction from the SPL Token 2022 program, which grants unlimited token allowance (U64_MAX) to a delegate account. The root cause of the vulnerability is the absence of a mechanism to revoke this allowance when the delegate admin changes the delegate account. As a result, even after a delegate is replaced (e.g., Alice is replaced by Bob), the old delegate (Alice) retains their full allowance. A malicious former delegate can exploit this by calling the `transfer` instruction using their still-active approval, thereby spending the remaining allowance and stealing tokens from the owner's account. This leads to direct theft of user funds, as the system provides no way to invalidate old approvals, leaving them active indefinitely on-chain.
